. Mother Amy, To payment of taxes for year 1922 on
                                                                                                  ...        $949 39
Block 69, District Lot 271, North Vancouver

In each case the tax bills are made out as against Marie Chaminade.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, OTTAWA, July 10, 1923.

DEAR MR. KEARNS, - I have your letter of the 27th ultimo, with reference to certain payments made by this
Department in connection with the Squamish Indian Boarding School in North Vancouver.

In reply I wish to state that this school is situated within the Municipality of North Vancouver, on property not owned
by the Government. It is maintained by a per capita grant, paid from Parliamentary appropriation. Representations
were made to the Department that owing to the situation of the school the financial aid so derived was inadequate. I
decided, therefore, to relieve them of taxation, which would place this school in the same position as an institution
located on an Indian reserve. We therefore purchased Block 123, District Lot 271, North Vancouver, from the
Reverend Sisters, and as it is now Government property, it is non-taxable, and we have assumed the payment of the
taxes on Lot 69, on which the school buildings are situated.

Yours very truly,
DUNCAN C. SCOTT, Deputy Supt. General.

The Assistant Auditor General, Ottawa.

Information requested with regard to Indian Schools

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, March 22, 1923.

SIR, - I have to request that you furnish me with a list of the various Indian Industrial, and Boarding Schools,
maintained or assisted by your Department, giving the amount of the annual per capita grant in each case, the
maximum number of pupils for which that grant is payable, and the denomination under whose auspices each school is
operated, distinguishing between government owned and church owned schools. I should like to get this information
for the fiscal year 1922 - 23 and to be advised with regard to any changes that may be made in the future.

At the same time I should like to be informed as to what part of the expenses of the various schools is supposed to be
covered by the annual grant, what expenses are considered as properly payable by the Government in addition to the
grant, and what expenses, if any, are supposed to be met by the religious body under whose auspices the school is
operated.

I am sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, December 28, 1923.

SIR, - I beg to refer you to my letter of March 22nd last, asking to be supplied with a list of the various Indian
Industrial and Boarding schools, together with certain information in connection therewith. As the list of schools and
other information desired has not yet been received, I have to renew my request for the same.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

Suggesting Separate Appropriation for Erection or Purchase of New Schools

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, March 22, 1923.

SIR, - In an application recently received by me for the issue of a cheque for the amount of $48,000 for the purchase
of the Kenora Boarding School from the Rev. Oblate Fathers, it was stated that that amount was included in your
estimates for the current year. As no such specific amount was voted for that purpose, I infer that it was included in
your general vote for Indian Education, and I also understand that the same vote was supposed to include an amount of
$75,000 towards the erection of a new school in the vicinity of Edmonton.

1 - 17 1/2 I

<!-- page 611 -->
Your total expenditure under the head of Indian Education appears to me to be naturally divisible into two heads, viz:
(1) the maintenance of existing schools and (2) the acquisition of school buildings either by purchase or by erection by
the department. As these two classes of expenditure are of an entirely different nature, might I suggest that it would be
advisable in future, when preparing your estimates, to ask separate amounts for the maintenance of the schools and for
the erection or purchase of new schools.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, OTTAWA, March 26, 1923.

DEAR MR. KEARNS, - I have your letter of the 22nd instant, with general reference to Parliamentary Appropriation
for Indian Education. Careful consideration will be given to your suggestion that separate votes be asked for the
maintenance of Indian Schools and for the erection, or purchase, of new schools.

Yours very truly,
DUNCAN C. SCOTT, Deputy Supt. General.

WM. KEARNS, Asst. Auditor General, Ottawa.

Payment of Share of Estate from Quebec Indian Lands
AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, December 7, 1923.

SIR, - The following cheques were issued during the fiscal year 1922 - 23 against the Province of Quebec Fund, Trust
Account No. 74, in settlement of the claim of Mrs. Mary Montour for her share of the estate of her father, Isaac Claus:
-

No. 2213. June 27, 1922 $100 00
No. 2712. July 12, 1922 100 00
No. 2834 July 21, 1922 800 00
Total     ...           $1,000 00

It appears that the estate consisted of a location on an Indian reserve with the improvements thereon; that Isaac Claus
died intestate and that, consequently, his son, Thomas Claus, and his daughter, Mrs. Mountour, were entitled to share
equally in the estate. It further appears that the property was purchased, for the sum of $2,000, by your department in
pursuance of the Soldier Settlement provisions of the Indian Act, but that in making settlement, the right of Mrs.
Mountour to a moiety of the estate was overlooked and the whole of the purchase money paid to the son, Thomas
Claus, who, it is understood, has left the country.

I understand that the Province of Quebec Fund was intended for the payment of the salaries of teachers and
missionaries, and for the relief of distress,

<!-- page 612 -->
especially among the unorganized Indians of the province. I do not consider that that fund, nor any part of it, should
have been used to correct an error made by your department. As the whole proceeds of the sale of the estate had been
paid over to the brother, Thomas Claus, there were no funds left in the hands of your department from which to pay
Mrs. Mountour's share, and the only way, in my opinion, by which she could be legally paid was to obtain a special
vote of Parliament for the amount of her share.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

Greater Production Scheme: Work continued after Cancellation of the Authority for the same

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, February 23, 1923.

SIR, - On January 16, 1922, an Order in Council (P.C. 82) was passed rescinding from that date the Order in Council
of February 16th, 1918 (P.C. 393), relative to the scheme for Greater Production on Indian Reserves and to the
appointment of Mr. W.M. Graham as Commissioner for carrying on that work.

I find, however, that, notwithstanding the rescinding of the original Order in Council, the Greater Production activities
have been continued all through the year 1922, although not to as great an extent as before.

Kindly advise me as to your authority for continuing this work after the passing of the Order in Council of January
16th, 1922.

I am, Sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, OTTAWA, February 26, 1923.

DEAR SIR, - I am in receipt of your letter of the 23rd instant, with reference to the Greater Production activities of
this department.

When the original Order in Council was cancelled it was believed that we could close the operations immediately, but
such has not been the case. I will write to the Indian Commissioner at Regina and ask him to outline for my
information the present position of these farming industries, and if it is necessary to continue any of them for any
length of time, I shall endeavour to obtain proper authority.

Yours very truly,
DUNCAN C. SCOTT, Deputy Supt. General.

WM. KEARNS, Asst. Auditor General, Ottawa.

<!-- page 613 -->
AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, December 28, 1923.

SIR, - I beg to refer you to my letter of February 23rd last and your reply thereto of February 26th, with regard to the
continuance of activities under the Greater Production Scheme after the passing of the Order in Council of January
16th, 1922, which rescinded the authority for carrying on that work.

Although the authority for carrying on the Greater Production Scheme was cancelled as from January 16th, 1922, the
activities were continued to a certain degree during the season of 1922 and again, in a somewhat less extent, during the
season of 1923. The moneys received after the cancellation of authority were dealt with in the same way as before, Mr.
Graham depositing all receipts to his credit in a special account at Regina and making all payments in connection with
the work from that account. As the special authority originally conferred on Mr. Graham under the War Measures Act
was removed by the cancelling Order in Council of January 16th, 1922, I consider that the further continuance of this
scheme was contrary to the provisions of the Consolidated Revenue and Audit Act which provides (Sect. 35) that "All
public moneys, from whatever source of revenue derived, shall be paid to the credit of the account of the Minister of
Finance and Receiver General," and further (.Sect. 41) that "The Auditor General shall see that no cheque issues for
the payment of any public money for which there is no direct parliamentary appropriation."

I am of opinion that Mr. Graham should be required to transmit forthwith for deposit to the credit of the Receiver
General all moneys now in his hands in connection with the Greater Production Scheme, and further to remit, from
time to time as they may be received, any moneys that may accrue hereafter from the sale of grain, equipment, etc. If it
is considered advisable to continue the scheme along the same lines the coming year it will be necessary to obtain
parliamentary authority for its continuance.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

Greater Production Scheme - Interest on other Trust Accounts Transposed to Greater Production Account

AUDIT OFFICE, December 21, 1923.

SIR, - In examining the statements rendered by Mr. W.M. Graham in connection with the Greater Production Scheme,
I find that he has credited the Greater Production Account with the interest allowed by the bank on the amounts on
deposit in two other of his Trust Accounts, viz: Grazing Leases Account and Indian Bands Trust Account. The first of
these accounts consists of the amounts collected for the lease of Indian lands, which amounts are ultimately distributed
among the Indians or transmitted to the department to be placed to the credit of the bands concerned. The second
account consists chiefly of amounts received from your department for distribution to the Indians.

When Mr. Reid of this office visited the Regina office last summer he was given to understand by Mr. Graham that the
reason that the interest accruing
